summary: The Welsh government has given more than £4m to the scheme since 2015, but will end it due to budget pressures.

summary: Colorado-based Leap is looking at the spaceport near Tongue as its first launch site outside of the US.

stories.title: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years
summary: Scientists have discovered chemically confirmed traces of ancient blood inside 115-million-year-old dinosaur bones, challenging assumptions about how long biological molecules can survive.
The extraordinary preservation could unlock new clues about dinosaur physiology and even help scientists search for ancient life elsewhere in the universe.

stories.title: Could you live on a remote island as a job?
summary: The new manager will start each workday surrounded by nature at the island wildlife reserve.

stories.title: Five-inch-long beetle larvae are quietly destroying blueberry roots
summary: Scientists have solved a mystery surrounding destructive beetles attacking blueberry bushes in North Carolina, identifying a species whose massive larvae can grow up to five inches long and destroy plant roots.
Although farmers have reported damage for more than a decade, the insects responsible remained unidentified until researchers used DNA analysis to uncover the culprit.

stories.title: Don't miss: Meteor showers, fireballs, and a supermoon light up November's night sky
summary: November's night sky is packed with celestial wonders, from bright meteor fireballs and a close pairing of Mars and Jupiter to a spectacular supermoon.
Meanwhile, NASA's Voyager 1 is making history by becoming the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth.

stories.title: NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space
summary: After nearly 22 years of exploring the universe’s most violent explosions, NASA’s Swift Observatory has re-entered Earth’s atmosphere over Indonesia.
Originally designed to last just two years, the pioneering space telescope transformed our understanding of black holes, exploding stars, and mysterious cosmic outbursts.

stories.title: 'Extra special' tamarin twins born at zoo
summary: Shaldon Wildlife Trust says it is one of two European zoos to breed the species in 2026.

stories.title: Dead stars could break one of physics' most famous limits
summary: A surprising new discovery suggests that some dead stars can grow far more massive than scientists once thought possible.
Computer simulations show that powerful magnetic fields could allow white dwarfs to reach 2.4 times the mass of the Sun, dramatically exceeding a famous limit that has stood for decades.
The findings could help explain unusually bright supernova explosions that have long puzzled astronomers.

stories.title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?
summary: An unprecedented early weakening of the polar vortex is causing uncertainty amongst experts over the impact it will have on UK weather as Simon King explains.

stories.title: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin
summary: A surprising new study suggests that an anti-aging drug could help protect people genetically predisposed to Alzheimer's disease.

Researchers found that just four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged adults carrying the high-risk APOE4 gene variant, with women showing the strongest benefits.
Because declining blood flow can occur years before Alzheimer's symptoms appear, the discovery raises hopes for preventing or delaying the disease before memory loss begins.

stories.title: Scientists discover that a clogged filter could revolutionize oil refining
summary: Scientists have developed a remarkable new membrane that separates crude oil at room temperature, using the oil itself to create microscopic filtration channels.

The breakthrough could cut refining energy consumption by nearly 32%, carbon emissions by almost 38%, and operating costs by 36%, potentially transforming one of the world's most energy-intensive industries.

stories.title: 400,000-year-old teeth reveal a stunning twist in human evolution
summary: A groundbreaking discovery is rewriting the story of human evolution, revealing that an ancient human species once thought to be an evolutionary dead end may have left genetic traces in people alive today.

By extracting proteins from 400,000-year-old Homo erectus teeth discovered in China, scientists uncovered evidence suggesting that these early humans interbred with Denisovans, another mysterious ancient human group.
That genetic connection may have eventually reached modern populations in the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and other parts of Southeast Asia.

stories.title: Scientists discover mysterious “lonely” brain waves linked to memory loss
summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising link between Alzheimer’s-related protein buildup, disrupted brain waves during deep sleep, and fading memory.
The findings suggest that hidden changes in how the brain processes memories overnight may contribute to age-related memory loss long before Alzheimer’s symptoms appear.

stories.title: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation
summary: Scientists have solved a decades-old mystery and uncovered a hidden immune system defense that protects healthy cells from the very inflammation meant to fight infections.
The surprising discovery could lead to new approaches for treating cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, and other conditions involving excessive inflammation.
